title.suggested: Allen Knocks Out Jim Egan at His Free and Easy

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported that Allen knocked out Jim Egan, once keeper of the Canterbury, in a quarrel at his free-and-easy, then drew a pistol on Egan's dog but put it away and had the men ejected.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Monday, October 29, 1883, page 2.

facts.fact: A short time before Oct. 29, 1883, a couple of thugs jumped Allen and tried to rob him, thinking he was past his prime, after a rumor that he had grown stiff and short of wind

Allen knocked out Jim Egan, who once kept the Canterbury, in a quarrel at his free-and-easy; Egan's friend Brooks grabbed Allen's hand and Egan's dog bit his trousers, Allen drew his pistol on the dog but put it away, and Egan and his friends were ejected

notes: Brawl was about two days before the paper date.
